title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21

ai_review.summary: Lively audience tape with a clear, crowd‑filled sound that captures an early‑1970 set highlighted by a haunting “He Was A Friend Of Mine” and a vibrant Viola Lee Blues > The Seven, despite occasional channel wobble.
ai_review.review: This audience recording (AUD) delivers the raw energy of a 1970 show – the crowd is audible and enthusiastic, and the set includes rare early performances such as “Friend of the Devil,” “Walking the Dog,” and a standout “He Was A Friend Of Mine.” The audio is generally listenable and even praised as one of the cleaner audience sources, though reviewers note right‑channel wavering, a bass‑heavy mix, muddy vocals and a brief tape‑curl that benefit from EQ and slight pitch correction.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give high marks (5‑star) and praise the performance; only a few note recording flaws, leading to an overall strong rating with solid confidence from seven detailed reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear crowd ambience, but right‑channel wavering and bassy mix reported; muddy vocal texture on some tracks, brief tape‑curl at the start of Viola Lee Blues > The Seven, and a need for slight BAL/EQ and -1% pitch correction.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The early‑1970 set runs as a single long set, mixing rare folk material with familiar blues/rock numbers; crowd interaction is high and the band transitions smoothly through highlights such as Viola Lee Blues > The Seven and the late‑show acoustic vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His playing is described as both brilliant (haunting tone on “He Was A Friend Of Mine”) and uneven – "all over the place" at times.
band_member_comments.Phil: Solid bass work, notably the spontaneous Cumberland segue during The Seven, helping keep the flow tight.
